headline: Earnings dip on higher costs; summer demand cushions blow
summary_short: Pinnacle West's Q2 2026 net income fell 7.3% y/y to $178.6M ($1.43 diluted EPS, -9.5% y/y) as higher interest and depreciation costs offset revenue growth of 7.1% y/y to $1,455.7M on strong summer cooling demand.
summary_long: Revenue rose 7.1% y/y to $1,455.7M on early, sustained summer heat that lifted cooling demand -- residential customer growth of 2.1% and weather-normalized sales growth of 5.6%, with total sales up 9.6%. Operating income was roughly flat (-0.6% y/y) at $305.7M. Net income fell 7.3% y/y to $178.6M ($1.43 diluted EPS, -9.5% y/y) as higher interest charges, higher depreciation and amortization, and lower transmission revenue -- a combined roughly $14M drag -- more than offset favorable weather, customer growth, lower O&M, and lower taxes. Cash fell to $9.1M from $18.8M a year ago; long-term debt rose 14.9% y/y to $9,775.8M. Pinnacle West continues to estimate FY2026 weather-normalized diluted EPS of $4.55-$4.75, unchanged.

drivers.explanation: Company attributes higher revenue to early, sustained summer heat driving increased cooling demand, with 2.1% residential customer growth and 5.6% weather-normalized sales growth; total sales rose 9.6%.

Y/y decline of ~$14M driven by higher interest charges, higher depreciation and amortization, and lower transmission service revenue, partly offset by favorable weather, customer growth, lower O&M expense, and lower taxes.
EPS fell more (-9.5%) than net income (-7.3%) because diluted weighted-average shares outstanding rose 2.2% y/y (124.5M vs 121.9M), adding dilution beyond the earnings decline.

CEO Ted Geisler said results were within expectations despite the y/y decline, citing unusually early, sustained summer heat that drove higher energy demand and load growth, with residential cooling degree days up 7% y/y.
